n: In this lecture we study the general foundations of the analysis of narcotic substances. The outline is as follows: the aim and methods of the discipline, international conventions, the law of Uzbekistan, the lists of the Cabinet of Ministers, classification and terminology, and finally the detection times in urine. Key terms: narcotic drugs, that is ND, psychotropic substances, that is PS, precursors, circulation, Lists I-IV, narcomania and toxicomania. The appendices are on pp. 160-172: the Cabinet of Ministers resolution and the control lists.

t: Aim and significance of the discipline
n: First, the aim and significance of the discipline. The analysis of narcotic substances is a specialist subject in the pharmaceutical field, studying the properties of ND and PS and their fate in the body and the cadaver. The discipline deals with isolation from biological specimens or fluids, the development of new methods of analysis, and the determination of identity and quantity. Its main aim is to teach the detection of chronic and acute poisonings of various degrees, and measures for their prevention.

Let us consider the tasks of practical analytical examination. The first is to isolate ND and PS from physical evidence and biological specimens and prepare them for analysis. The second is to analyse the isolated substances by chemical and physicochemical methods and to complete the necessary documents. The third is to determine the identity and quantity of ND and PS in the extracts. The fourth is to apply rapid express methods of analysis to establish the causes in acute poisonings.

Now the tasks of the discipline. The first task is to develop methods of isolating ND and PS from samples and to improve existing ones. The second is to develop methods of purifying isolated samples from foreign substances. The third is to study the physical and chemical properties of ND, PS and precursors, and to develop sensitive, specific chemical and physicochemical methods. The fourth is to study the metabolism of ND and PS in the body and the methods of analysing them.

On the relevance of the problem. According to the UN, 18 million people in the world use heroin, and over 200 million use various narcotic substances. The First President, at the 48th session of the UN General Assembly, on 28 September 1993, called for stronger efforts against the drug trade. In addition, crimes involving narcotic drugs are increasing in developed countries. This shows the practical importance of the discipline.

Basic concepts: types of dependence. Drug addiction, that is narcomania, is a disease associated with psychological and physical dependence on narcotic drugs. Polynarcomania is the chronic use of two or more kinds of narcotic drugs. Toxicomania, that is substance abuse, is psychological and physical dependence on psychotropic substances that have no medicinal properties but act actively on the psyche. Remember: the difference lies in which substance, and how many substances, the dependence concerns.

We turn to the historical background. The use of narcotic substances has been known since ancient times: they were used in religious rites, in idol worship and in folk medicine. In Egypt, cannabis was used as a narcotic substance. Herodotus wrote that the nomads of Central Asia threw cannabis on the fire and became intoxicated by the smell. In the works of Hippocrates it is noted that Indian hemp was brought to Europe by the Scythians before the Trojan War. Ibn Sina, in volume 2 of the Canon of Medicine, pointed to the harmful effect of cannabis; these are articles 634 and 689.

The objects of the discipline fall into three groups. The first is plant products: cannabis, opium poppy and others, their extracts and samples. The second is solid substances, that is powders, tablets and dragees, as well as injection solutions. The third is biological samples: blood, urine, hair, nails, organs and others. That is, the analysis may begin from a plant, from a dosage form, or from a sample of the body.

Stages and methods of analysis. The stages are: sampling, purification from foreign substances, and qualitative and quantitative analysis. The methods fall into several groups. Chemical methods include colour and precipitation reactions. In the microcrystalloscopic method the shape of crystals is examined. The chromatographic methods include TLC, GLC, gel chromatography, HPLC and GC-MS. Photometric methods are PEC and UV and IR spectrophotometry. Fluorescence, biological methods, immunoassay and electrochemical methods are also used.

Links with other sciences. Pharmacology, narcology and toxicology study the effect of ND and PS on human and animal organs. In determining quality and quantity, the methods of analytical, organic and pharmaceutical chemistry are used. In studying metabolites, one relies on toxicological, biological, analytical and pharmaceutical chemistry. Because some plant products are the source of narcotic substances, the chemist must have a thorough knowledge of pharmacognosy.

UN conventions. In 1995 our country acceded to the following UN conventions. The 1961 convention concerns narcotic drugs, the 1971 convention psychotropic substances, and the 1988 convention the fight against illicit traffic. In addition, cooperation agreements have been signed with more than 30 states.

Cooperation and national legislation. Intergovernmental agreements have been concluded with Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, the USA, Turkey and Pakistan. On 19 August 1999 the Law on Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances was adopted. In accordance with the Presidential Decree No. PQ-175/2 of 15 December 2000, the National Information and Analytical Centre for Drug Control was established under the Cabinet of Ministers.

Criminal liability. Articles 270, 271, 273, 274, 275 and 276 of the Criminal Code are devoted to illicit circulation of ND or PS. Article 270 concerns the cultivation of prohibited crops, and Article 271 the illicit acquisition of ND or PS. Article 273 covers illicit preparation, receipt, storage and transport of ND or PS for the purpose of transport. Looking at the trend, in 1999-2000 the corresponding crimes rose by 17.9 per cent, and by 2003 they had fallen by 9.4 per cent.

t: Structure of the law: Sections I-III
n: The first part of the structure of the law. Law No. 813-I was drawn up in line with the three UN conventions. The law consists of 6 sections and 46 articles. Section I contains the general provisions and includes Articles 1-4. Section II is devoted to activity related to circulation, Articles 5-9. Section III sets the conditions for types of activity, Articles 10-23.

t: Structure of the law: Sections IV-VI
n: The second part of the structure of the law. Section IV regulates the use of ND, PS and precursors, Articles 24-32. Section V is devoted to preventing illicit circulation, Articles 33-43. Section VI concerns narcological care, Articles 44-46. Thus the law begins with general provisions and ends with narcological care.

Let us summarise the structure of the law. Law No. 813-I of 19 August 1999 consists of 6 sections and 46 articles. The law was drawn up in line with the three UN conventions of 1961, 1971 and 1988. The largest section is Section III, Articles 10-23, that is 14 articles. The smallest is Section VI, Articles 44-46, that is 3 articles.

Lists of controlled substances. According to Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 878 of 27 October 2018, substances are placed on four lists. List I contains prohibited ND, 246 in number. List II contains restricted ND, 51. List III contains restricted PS, 85. List IV contains restricted precursors, 29. The lists are approved by the Cabinet of Ministers in the established manner and published in the press.

t: Cabinet resolution: import, export and transit
n: The Cabinet of Ministers resolution regulates import, export and transit. The resolution lays down the procedure for bringing ND, PS and precursors into the territory of Uzbekistan, taking them out, and passing them in transit; this is No. 330 of 12 November 2015. A certificate is required for import or export, and a permit for transit. The procedure for obtaining a permit to place goods in a closed customs warehouse is also given in the appendices. The State Commission on Narcotic Drug Control strictly supervises compliance with the established procedure.

Contents of the resolution's appendices. Appendices 1-3 are regulations on the permit procedures for obtaining certificates and permits. Appendix 4 is List I, that is prohibited ND, and Appendix 5 is List II, that is restricted ND. Appendix 6 is List III, that is restricted PS, and Appendix 7 is List IV, that is restricted precursors. So each list has its own appendix.

Basic terms. Narcotic drugs, that is ND, are listed substances whose circulation is subject to control, and preparations and plants containing narcotic substances. Psychotropic substances, that is PS, are listed synthetic or natural substances whose circulation is subject to control. Precursors are substances used to prepare ND and PS and included in the list of precursors. Analogues are substances similar to ND and PS in structure and properties that act actively on the psyche.

The terms circulation and illicit acquisition. A preparation is a mixture, in any physical state, of substances containing one or more ND or PS. Circulation means import or export, transit, storage, sale, distribution, receipt, transport, production, use, destruction and cultivation of plants. Illicit acquisition is obtaining by theft, fraud, misappropriation, robbery, abuse of office, extortion or armed assault.

Sowing, cultivation and authorised bodies. Sowing of plants containing narcotic substances means scattering their seeds in specially prepared soil or planting out seedlings. Cultivation is the tending of plants sown on any land or that have sprouted on their own, that is watering, hoeing and fertilising. The specially authorised bodies exercise management and control in the sphere of circulation in accordance with the powers determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

Opiates and opioids. Opiates are ND similar in structure to morphine: morphine, codeine, heroin, that is diacetylmorphine, and its main metabolite 6-monoacetylmorphine, in short 6-MAM. Heroin is a potent narcotic drug synthesised from morphine by an acetylation reaction. Opioids are synthetic agents that act like morphine but belong to another group: promedol, methadone, fentanyl and others.

Structure of opium alkaloids. This group of alkaloids of narcological significance consists chiefly of the opium alkaloids. Their molecules contain an isoquinoline nucleus. By structure, two subgroups are distinguished: the first is phenanthrene-isoquinoline derivatives, and the second is benzylisoquinoline derivatives.

t: List I: opium and opioid groups
n: The opium and opioid groups of List I. Heroin, that is diacetylmorphine, 3-monoacetylmorphine and 6-monoacetylmorphine are on List I. Methadone, that is phenadone, pethidine, oxycodone, oxymorphone, hydromorphone, desomorphine and other opioids are also on this list. Likewise opium, that is medicinal opium, which is the juice of the poppy. Also included are the plant species Papaver somniferum L, acetylated opium, poppy straw and its extract.

t: List I: cannabis, coca, cathinone groups
n: The cannabis, coca and cathinone groups of List I. The cannabis group includes hashish, that is anasha or cannabis resin, cannabis, that is marijuana, cannabis oil and tetrahydrocannabinol, with all its isomers. The coca group has coca leaf, the cocaine shrub and ecgonine. Cathine, that is d-norpseudoephedrine, cathinone, that is l-alpha-aminopropiophenone, ephedrone and the KHAT plant are also on this list. Likewise products prepared from ephedrine and pseudoephedrine or from preparations containing them.

The synthetic substances of List I: amphetamines and hallucinogens. Methamphetamine, dexamphetamine, MDA, MDMA, MBDB, DOB, DMA, TMA, PMA and STP, that is DOM, are on this list. LSD, that is d-lysergide, and lysergic acid preparations, psilocin, psilocybin and mushrooms containing them are also included. Then mescaline, DMT, DET, phencyclidine, etryptamine and 2S-V, that is 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine.

The synthetic cannabinoids of List I. At the end of the list, cannabimimetics and similar compounds with laboratory codes are given: AM-2201, RCS-4, UR-144, AKB-48, CP-47,497 and others. There are also MAM-2201, WIN-55,212-2, CB-13, STS-135, 5FUR-144, URB-597, JTE-907 and others. According to Resolution No. 878 of 2018, List I, that is the list of prohibited ND, names 246 substances.

List II contains the restricted narcotic drugs. It has morphine, as the hydrochloride and sulphate, codeine phosphate, omnopon, cocaine hydrochloride, buprenorphine, butorphanol and pentazocine. Also fentanyl, alfentanil, sufentanil, remifentanil, trimeperidine, that is promedol, ethylmorphine, that is dionine, tilidine, thebaine and phenmetrazine. Also on this list are amobarbital, etaminal sodium, that is pentobarbital, glutethimide, amfepramone and levamfetamine.

List II also sets limits for preparations. Item 30 specifies preparations containing not more than 0.1% cocaine and not more than 0.2% morphine, that is, preparations combined with other ingredients from which the narcotic cannot easily be separated. In combined preparations, codeine in excess of 8 mg per solid dose, or in excess of 80 mg per 100 ml or 100 g of a liquid form. In diphenoxin preparations, not more than 0.5 mg of diphenoxin and atropine sulphate per dose; for diphenoxylate, not more than 2.5 mg.

The first part of List III. Barbiturates: barbital, barbital sodium, phenobarbital, allobarbital, butobarbital, butalbital, cyclobarbital and thiopental sodium. Benzodiazepines: diazepam, nitrazepam, chlordiazepoxide, oxazepam, phenazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam, lorazepam, midazolam and temazepam. Among other hypnotics and tranquillisers, meprobamate, zolpidem, GHB and sodium oxybutyrate are on this list.

The second part of List III. Ketamine, droperidol, halothane, clonidine hydrochloride, trihexyphenidyl hydrochloride and feprosidnine hydrochloride. Phentermine, fencamfamine, pyrovalerone, pemoline, pipradrol, mazindol, benzphetamine and etilamfetamine. Then ephedrine hydrochloride, pseudoephedrine and its combined medicinal products if there is more than 10 mg per dose, as well as levomethamphetamine and racemic methamphetamine.

List IV contains the chemical precursors. Each precursor is given with its synonyms, and for some a concentration limit is set. For example, acetone at 60% and above, and sulphuric acid at 45% and above, salts excepted. Hydrochloric acid at 15% and above, salts excepted. Toluene at 70% and above, and ethyl ether at 45% and above, come under control.

t: List IV: alkaloid and amine precursors
n: The alkaloid and amine precursors of List IV. Ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, phenylpropanolamine, that is norephedrine, and ephedra herb containing ephedrine. Ergotamine, ergometrine and lysergic acid, anthranilic acid and N-acetylanthranilic acid. Phenylacetic acid, phenyl-2-propanone, 3,4-methylenedioxyphenyl-2-propanone, safrole, isosafrole and piperonal. And also acetic anhydride, propionic anhydride, potassium permanganate, piperidine, methyl ethyl ketone and red phosphorus.

Detection times in urine. These data give the time intervals of detectability in urine after a single use, CDRH, 1997. Cannabinoids are detected after 1-3 hours and persist for 1-7 days. Heroin is detected after 2-6 hours, for 24-72 hours. Methamphetamine after 4-6 hours, for 48-72 hours. Cocaine after 2-6 hours, for 48-72 hours. Phencyclidine is detected 4-6 hours after use and may be found for 7-14 days.

To conclude. ND, PS and precursors are regulated by the UN conventions of 1961, 1971 and 1988, the Law of 1999 and Cabinet of Ministers resolutions. Controlled substances are divided into List I, prohibited ND, List II, restricted ND, List III, restricted PS, and List IV, restricted precursors. Review questions: what are ND, PS, a precursor, narcomania, toxicomania and polynarcomania? What are the objects and methods of the discipline? What international and national documents exist?

t: Review questions: the discipline and concepts
n: The first part of the review questions. What are the significance and tasks of the analysis of narcotic substances as a discipline? What substances are meant by narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and precursors? What are the objects of the discipline and the requirements placed on them, and what methods of analysis are used in it?

The second part of the review questions. Which international normative documents do you know, and what normative documents exist in Uzbekistan? What do you understand by narcomania? What do you understand by toxicomania? What is polynarcomania?
